description:
(Summary from jobright.ai; the original posting may say more.)

Datacor is hiring an early-career Software Engineer for its Flow Simulation team. The role builds and maintains fluid flow simulation applications, contributing across application features, modernization, tooling, testing, and defect resolution.
Software Engineer building and maintaining Windows desktop application features, fixing defects, and contributing to CI/CD and test infrastructure

Responsibilities:
• Design, build, and maintain features across all layers of our Windows desktop applications, working from requirements with guidance from senior engineers
• Diagnose and fix defects anywhere in the codebase, including customer-reported issues escalated from our Support team
• Contribute to internal tooling, build automation, CI/CD pipelines, and test infrastructure
• Take part in our ongoing modernization, including new architecture and user interface frameworks
• Write clean, maintainable, well-tested code, and take part in code reviews, both giving and receiving feedback
• Share team responsibilities such as build pipeline and bug-triage rotations
• Collaborate with engineers, QA, Product Management, and domain experts to deliver solutions that meet user needs
• Stay on top of industry trends, and use modern tools, including AI coding assistants, responsibly to continuously improve your skillset

Requirements:
• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience)
• 0–2 years of professional software development experience; internships, co-ops, and substantial academic or personal projects count
• Proficiency in at least one object-oriented language, preferably C# (VB.NET, Java, or C++ also welcome)
• Solid grounding in computer science fundamentals: object-oriented design, data structures, and algorithms
• Working knowledge of version control, including branching, commits, and merging
• Demonstrated ability to write clean, readable, and maintainable code
• Strong problem-solving and debugging skills, and the judgment to ask for help when stuck
• Excellent communication and collaboration skills

Preferred:
• Experience with the .NET ecosystem and Visual Studio
• Exposure to user interface development, whether desktop (WPF, WinForms) or web
• Experience writing unit tests or working with automated testing
• Familiarity with scripting languages such as Python or PowerShell
• Experience with Git, including pull requests and code reviews
• Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines, Agile practices, or tools such as Jira and Bitbucket
• Familiarity with data serialization (JSON, XML) or multi-threading concepts
• Experience using AI coding assistants thoughtfully, including verifying the code they produce
• Interest in engineering, scientific, or simulation software
